lesson.title: Singular value decomposition

steps.headline: Every matrix splits as A = U Σ Vᵀ: one stretch between two length-preserving turns.

lead.text: U and V are orthogonal, so they only rotate or reflect. Σ is diagonal and holds the stretch sizes, called singular values. They are never negative, and the number of positive ones equals the rank.
A = $\begin{pmatrix}3&0\\0&-2\end{pmatrix}$ stretches across by 3 and up by 2, and flips up. Singular values record only the sizes of the stretches.

reveal.text: You compared the sizes of the stretches and ignored the flip. Singular values measure size only.

workedSteps.text: The two columns are perpendicular. Their lengths are the stretch sizes.
The minus sign is a flip, so it goes into U. Σ keeps only the sizes.

steps.headline: Find the smaller singular value of $\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\2&4\end{pmatrix}$.

workedSteps.text: The second row is twice the first, so the rank is 1.
The number of positive singular values equals the rank. What is the smaller singular value?

lead.text: The matrix is $\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\0&2&0\end{pmatrix}$. It has two nonzero stretches, one per row.

reveal.text: You read the stretches off the matrix and took the smaller. Singular values are usually listed from the largest to the smallest.

lead.text: A 2 × 3 matrix takes three inputs to two outputs. In the full SVD, Σ has the same shape as A, with the singular values along its diagonal.

lesson.orientation: Separate a rectangular map into orthogonal coordinate changes and nonnegative stretches.
lesson.nextAction: Try the next idea, then return for a fresh problem after a delay.

blocks.text: A machine stretches every vector across by 4 and up by 2, then spins the whole plane a quarter turn.

intro.promise: By the end you'll split any matrix into two length-preserving turns and one stretch, and read its singular values.

recap.keyIdea: Every matrix is A = U Σ Vᵀ. U and Vᵀ preserve length, and Σ holds the nonnegative singular values: the stretches. The number of positive ones is the rank.

blocks.text: You read the largest singular value of diag(3, −2) as 3, found that a rank-one matrix has a singular value of 0, and matched the shape of Σ to A.

recap.nextHook: That completes the course. Review these ideas later and a fresh problem will bring them back.

answerAuthority.workedAnswer: The turn keeps lengths, so the longest output comes from the biggest stretch: 4.

questions.prompt: What is the longest an output can be for an input of length 1?
hints: A quarter turn changes direction, not length.
Which of the two stretches is bigger?
The best input lies along the biggest stretch.

misconceptions.feedback: That multiplies the two stretches. One arrow feels only the stretch along its own direction.

questions.onCorrect: 4. The turn does not change length, so the largest stretch sets the longest output. That is the largest singular value.

answerAuthority.workedAnswer: The column lengths are 7 and 2, so the largest singular value is 7.

questions.prompt: What is the largest singular value of $\begin{pmatrix}-7&0\\0&2\end{pmatrix}$?
hints: The columns are perpendicular. How long is each?
Singular values are never negative.
Take the longer of the two lengths.

misconceptions.feedback: That is the entry with its sign. Singular values are never negative.
That is the smaller stretch. The question asks for the largest.

questions.onCorrect: The minus sign is a flip. The stretch size is 7.

questions.prompt: What is the largest singular value of A = $\begin{pmatrix}3&0\\0&-2\end{pmatrix}$?
hints: The columns are perpendicular. How long is each?
Ignore the signs, because a flip is not a stretch.
Take the longer of the two lengths.

answerAuthority.workedAnswer: The two stretch magnitudes are 3 and 2, so the largest singular value is 3.

misconceptions.feedback: That is the smaller stretch. The question asks for the largest.

questions.onCorrect: The stretch sizes are 3 and 2. The sign of the second is just a flip.

acceptedIdeas: A flip is carried by U or V, so Σ holds only stretch sizes.
answerAuthority.exampleAnswer: U and V can reflect, which handles any flip. Σ then needs only sizes.

questions.prompt: Why is a singular value never negative?

choices.label: A flip is carried by U or V, so Σ holds only stretch sizes.
Negative stretches would make the matrix invertible.
Singular values are always larger than the entries.

hints: Which factors can flip, and which stretch?

misconceptions.feedback: Invertibility depends on whether any singular value is zero, not on signs.
They need not be: for a diagonal matrix they equal the sizes of the entries.

questions.onCorrect: U and V can reflect, so any flip lives there. Σ holds only the stretch sizes.

questions.prompt: What is the smaller singular value of A = $\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\2&4\end{pmatrix}$?
hints: What is the rank of A?
The number of positive singular values equals the rank.
How many singular values does a two-by-two matrix have?

answerAuthority.workedAnswer: The matrix has rank one, so its second singular value is zero.

misconceptions.feedback: That is the larger singular value. The question asks for the smaller one.

questions.onCorrect: Rank one means one positive singular value. The other is zero: the map flattens the plane to a line.

questions.prompt: What is the smaller singular value of A = $\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\0&2&0\end{pmatrix}$?
hints: Which entries are the nonzero stretches?
Each row stretches along its own axis.
Take the smaller of the two stretches.

answerAuthority.workedAnswer: The two nonzero stretch factors are 2 and 1; the smaller is 1.

misconceptions.feedback: That is the larger singular value. The question asks for the smaller one.

questions.onCorrect: The two nonzero stretches are 2 and 1, so the smaller singular value is 1.

questions.prompt: For a 2 × 3 matrix A, what is the shape of Σ in the full SVD?
hints: Σ must map the same inputs to the same outputs as A.

answerAuthority.exampleAnswer: Σ has the same shape as A: 2 × 3.

misconceptions.feedback: That would drop an input. Σ takes the same three inputs as A to the same two outputs.
That would add an output. Σ has the same shape as A.

questions.onCorrect: Σ takes the same inputs to the same outputs, so it has A's shape.

questions.prompt: Which SVD factor performs the nonnegative stretching?
hints: Which factor is diagonal?

answerAuthority.exampleAnswer: Σ holds the singular values. U and Vᵀ only turn.

misconceptions.feedback: U is orthogonal, so it only rotates or reflects.
Vᵀ is orthogonal, so it only rotates or reflects.

questions.onCorrect: Σ is the diagonal stretch. U and Vᵀ preserve length.

questions.prompt: What is the largest singular value of A = $\begin{pmatrix}0&5\\2&0\\0&0\end{pmatrix}$?
hints: The two columns are perpendicular. How long is each?
Ignore the zero row.
Take the longer of the two lengths.

answerAuthority.workedAnswer: The column directions are perpendicular with lengths 2 and 5; the largest stretch is 5.

misconceptions.feedback: That is the smaller stretch. The question asks for the largest.
That adds the two lengths. A stretch is measured along one direction.

questions.onCorrect: The columns are perpendicular, with lengths 2 and 5. The longest is the largest singular value.

answerAuthority.workedAnswer: The column lengths are 3 and 8, so the smaller singular value is 3.

questions.prompt: What is the smaller singular value of A = $\begin{pmatrix}-3&0\\0&-8\end{pmatrix}$?
hints: The columns are perpendicular. How long is each?
Singular values are never negative.
Take the shorter of the two lengths.

misconceptions.feedback: That is the entry with its sign. Singular values are never negative.
That is the larger singular value. The question asks for the smaller one.

questions.onCorrect: Both signs are flips. The stretch sizes are 3 and 8, and the smaller is 3.
